About us

What began as a dream is now a reality.

Established in 2021, CGA resulted from untainted, consistent hard work — a union of educators who believe in empowering the next generation of leaders.

Cambridge O Level, IGCSE and A Level preparation in Lahore — built on method, discipline and small classes.

Vision

To be a beacon of educational excellence, recognised internationally for producing well-rounded leaders equipped with Cambridge qualifications and a profound sense of responsibility.

Mission

Empowering future leaders through a transformative education that cultivates critical thinking, creativity and resilience within the framework of the Cambridge system.

Core values

Academic excellence, community engagement and innovation — the values held to maintain school tradition.

Known for

Examiner’s edge. 93% A & A*. Small classes. Honest feedback. Seven floors. Since 2021.

Major modules offered

Eight ways in. One standard.

The modules our students are in favour of learning currently — each with its own calendar, checkpoints and reporting rhythm.

  • 2 Years

    Fast Track Pre O Levels

    Grade 6 to 8 compressed into two years — entry test, MBTI and career counselling, two-weekly testing and seven promotional exams.

  • 2 Years

    Private O Levels

    A controlled two-year run to CAIEs: notes and topicals handed over on day one, mocks in March, support right up to exam day.

  • 2 Years

    Private A Levels

    AS then A2, same rhythm — two-weekly testing, yearlies, intensive past-paper prep leave and online support until the last paper.

  • 5 Months

    Evening O/A Level Course

    July to December, starting from scratch. Updated notes, targeted topicals, exam-style questions and one-on-one attention.

  • 3 Months

    Evening Crash Course

    July–Sep or Jan–Apr. Fast-pace coverage for students who need the whole syllabus tightened before the exam.

  • One on one

    Helping Cubicles

    Customised, student-wise plans for those who need special attention — digging into the loopholes and rebuilding confidence.

  • 2 Months

    Entry Test Preps

    SAT, IELTS, MDCAT, NET and NTS — university selection, admission criteria, deadlines, mock tests and placements.

  • 3 Months

    Life Skills & Self Defence

    A weekend programme built into the curriculum: gym and martial arts, leadership workshops and community service.

The four stages

From a first diagnostic to a final A*.

Nobody walks in with an A*. It is assembled, stage by stage, on a fixed timetable — and every student runs the same four stages, whichever module they join.

  1. 1Diagnosis

    We find out where they actually are

    An entry evaluation, an MBTI profile and a proper counselling sitting — before a single subject is picked.

    • Entry test in maths, English and science reasoning
    • Subject fit discussed with parents, not assumed
    • Career direction mapped to the subject combination
  2. 2Method

    Then they get the material that works

    Our own compiled notes and topicals on day one, taught in the wording Cambridge examiners are trained to reward.

    • Complete Guide notes, updated for 2026–2028
    • Topical worksheets after every chapter
    • Marking taught from the mark scheme itself
  3. 3Pressure

    Then we make the exam boring

    Two-weekly tests, seven promotional exams and full mocks in March, so the real paper is the least surprising day of the year.

    • Two-weekly progress tests, reported to parents
    • Timed past-paper sessions under exam conditions
    • Helping cubicles for whatever the test exposed
  4. 4The paper

    Then they sit it — and it shows

    500+ CAIE appearances, 93% of them graded A or A*, and 40+ students carried into further study on scholarships.

    • 93% A and A* in the May 2026 O Levels
    • Nine-A* result sheets, more than once
    • Support that continues right up to results day

Four things we do that most places don’t

These are the four parts of the week every student actually feels.

Small classes

Every student is a name, not a seat.

Classes stay small enough that a teacher notices the day a student goes quiet. One-on-one attention is scheduled into the week, not offered when a parent complains.

Helping Cubicles

A desk to sit at until it makes sense.

Stuck on a topic after class? The cubicles are open with a teacher on hand — no appointment, no extra fee, no waiting for the next lesson to ask.

Examiner’s edge

Marked the way Cambridge marks it.

A serving Cambridge O Level examiner sits behind every mark scheme our students work from — so a correction here is the same correction the examiner would have made.

Beyond the syllabus

Gym, martial arts, life skills, service.

Seven floors means room for more than classrooms. Physical fitness, self defence, leadership workshops and community service run alongside the academic calendar.

Life Skills & P.E

A curriculum for the rest of life.

  • Cooking with minimal resources
  • Self defence
  • Public speaking
  • Stitching
  • House maintenance and repairs
  • Survival training
  • Financial literacy
  • Moral conscious development
  • Hygiene

Before you ask

Questions parents ask us most.

Which modules and levels do you offer?

Cambridge O Level, IGCSE, AS and A2 — through eight modules: Fast Track Pre O Levels, Private O Levels, Private A Levels, five-month evening courses, three-month crash courses, Helping Cubicles, entry test prep and the Life Skills programme.

What is the Fast Track Pre O Level programme?

Grade 6 to 8 compressed into two years. It starts with an entry test, MBTI personality testing and career counselling, then runs on two-weekly testing, progress reports and seven promotional exams — saving a full year, and a substantial sum, against the conventional route.

Is the assessment really free?

Yes. Bring your child in, meet the teachers, and get an honest read on where they stand — topic by topic. No cost, no obligation.

What are the fees?

Fees vary by module — morning O Level batches, evening courses, Helping Cubicles and entry test prep are all priced differently. Message us on WhatsApp at 0302 9255003 for the current schedule; the figures in our comparison section are indicative 2025–26 approximations.

How often are students tested?

Two-weekly progress tests throughout, mid-terms, yearlies, mocks in March–April, and intensive past-paper practice during prep leave — with progress reports and parent–teacher discussions at every checkpoint.

What are Helping Cubicles?

One-to-one classes for students who need special attention or want to fast-track. Each student gets a personalised academic plan and testing schedule, in a more focused session.

Do you provide notes and past papers?

Yes — notes and topicals are handed over at enrolment, and our “Complete Guide — Notes” series is compiled in-house. You can also buy the books without enrolling.

What happens after results?

Academic counselling, a parent–teacher meeting, high-achiever encouragement, and support with university applications through the entry test prep module.

Where are you located?

Building 1133, F Commercial, State Life Society, Lahore. Office hours 10:00–20:00.
